geo-1-hazards-risk-and-disasters.title: Hazards, risk and disasters
geo-1-hazards-risk-and-disasters.coverage: Lesson concept checks followed by related subject revision.

questions.prompt: Hazards, risk and disasters — Which statement accurately explains hazards, risk and disasters?
options: A hazard is a potentially damaging process; risk depends on the chance of an event and its consequences for exposed people and assets. A disaster is a severe disruption when impacts exceed a community’s capacity to cope.
A severe hazard always creates the same disaster everywhere.
A place’s name alone establishes its processes and outcomes.
questions.explanation: Exposure locates people or assets in harm’s way; vulnerability describes susceptibility; capacity includes resources to prepare and recover. The same physical event can produce different losses in two places.

questions.prompt: Hazards, risk and disasters — Which statement is a misconception to correct?
options: Methods should be appropriate to the question and data.
A severe hazard always creates the same disaster everywhere.
A supported conclusion should identify its evidence and scope.
questions.explanation: A hazard is a potentially damaging process; risk depends on the chance of an event and its consequences for exposed people and assets. A disaster is a severe disruption when impacts exceed a community’s capacity to cope. Exposure locates people or assets in harm’s way; vulnerability describes susceptibility; capacity includes resources to prepare and recover. The same physical event can produce different losses in two places.

questions.explanation: Reasoning needs appropriate geographical scale, comparable definitions and acknowledgement of uncertainty. In this lesson: hazard.

geo-1-atmospheric-hydrological-and-geomo.title: Atmospheric, hydrological and geomorphic hazards
geo-1-atmospheric-hydrological-and-geomo.coverage: Lesson concept checks followed by related subject revision.

questions.prompt: Atmospheric, hydrological and geomorphic hazards — Which statement accurately explains atmospheric, hydrological and geomorphic hazards?
options: Atmospheric hazards arise from weather processes; hydrological hazards involve water movement or availability; geomorphic hazards involve Earth materials and landforms. Boundaries can overlap in a compound event.
Each event belongs to one isolated category with no linked hazards.
A place’s name alone establishes its processes and outcomes.
questions.explanation: A tropical cyclone is atmospheric, river flooding is hydrological and a landslide is geomorphic. Drought develops through prolonged water shortage; bushfire involves fuel, weather and ignition rather than a single category alone.

questions.prompt: Atmospheric, hydrological and geomorphic hazards — Which statement is a misconception to correct?
options: Methods should be appropriate to the question and data.
Each event belongs to one isolated category with no linked hazards.
A supported conclusion should identify its evidence and scope.

geo-1-ecological-hazards-and-transmissio.title: Ecological hazards and transmission pathways
geo-1-ecological-hazards-and-transmissio.coverage: Lesson concept checks followed by related subject revision.

questions.prompt: Ecological hazards and transmission pathways — Which statement accurately explains ecological hazards and transmission pathways?
options: Ecological hazards include biological threats such as infectious disease, invasive animals and water-borne illness, and chemical contamination. Identify the agent, pathway and exposed population.
Every disease after a flood is transmitted through drinking water.
A place’s name alone establishes its processes and outcomes.
questions.explanation: Infection can spread through contact, vectors or contaminated water. An invasive species can disrupt food webs; chemicals may move through runoff and bioaccumulate. A hazard becomes a risk where a pathway links an agent to people or ecosystems.

questions.prompt: Ecological hazards and transmission pathways — Which statement is a misconception to correct?
options: Methods should be appropriate to the question and data.
Every disease after a flood is transmitted through drinking water.
A supported conclusion should identify its evidence and scope.

geo-1-magnitude-duration-and-spatial-ext.title: Magnitude, duration and spatial extent
geo-1-magnitude-duration-and-spatial-ext.coverage: Lesson concept checks followed by related subject revision.

questions.prompt: Magnitude, duration and spatial extent — Which statement accurately explains magnitude, duration and spatial extent?
options: Magnitude measures event intensity or size; duration is how long it lasts; spatial extent is the area affected. Frequency describes occurrence over time, while probability expresses likelihood within a stated period.
The event with the greatest intensity must have the greatest total impact.
A place’s name alone establishes its processes and outcomes.
questions.explanation: A high category cyclone may have a small intense core but widespread rain. A long drought may have lower daily intensity yet large cumulative losses. Never compare events using a category number alone.

questions.prompt: Magnitude, duration and spatial extent — Which statement is a misconception to correct?
options: Methods should be appropriate to the question and data.
The event with the greatest intensity must have the greatest total impact.
A supported conclusion should identify its evidence and scope.

questions.prompt: Recurrence intervals and probability — Which statement accurately explains recurrence intervals and probability?
options: A recurrence interval is a long-run average interval between events at or above a specified magnitude; it is not a timetable. A 1-in-100-year event has a 1% annual exceedance probability under the assumed stationary model.
A 50-year flood cannot happen again until 50 years have passed.
A place’s name alone establishes its processes and outcomes.
questions.explanation: For independent years with constant annual probability p, the chance of at least one event in n years is 1 − (1 − p)^n. Climate or land-use changes can invalidate a stationary estimate.

questions.prompt: Where hazards occur and why — Which statement accurately explains where hazards occur and why?

A map of losses is the same as a map of physical hazard frequency.
A place’s name alone establishes its processes and outcomes.
questions.explanation: Earthquakes often cluster near plate boundaries; tropical cyclones need warm oceans and suitable atmospheric conditions; disease patterns reflect climate, vectors, mobility and surveillance. Exposure patterns may differ from hazard patterns.

geo-1-eastings-northings-and-grid-refere.title: Eastings, northings and grid references
geo-1-eastings-northings-and-grid-refere.coverage: Lesson concept checks followed by related subject revision.

questions.prompt: Eastings, northings and grid references — Which statement accurately explains eastings, northings and grid references?
options: Grid references identify positions on a mapped grid. Read eastings first, then northings. A four-figure area reference identifies a square; a six-figure reference estimates a point to tenths within it.
Northings are read before eastings.
A place’s name alone establishes its processes and outcomes.
questions.explanation: For a six-figure reference, interpolate within the square rather than reading the upper-right grid line. Accuracy depends on grid scale and symbol position. Preserve leading zeroes when present.

questions.prompt: Eastings, northings and grid references — Which statement is a misconception to correct?
options: Methods should be appropriate to the question and data.
Northings are read before eastings.
A supported conclusion should identify its evidence and scope.
questions.explanation: Grid references identify positions on a mapped grid. Read eastings first, then northings. A four-figure area reference identifies a square; a six-figure reference estimates a point to tenths within it. For a six-figure reference, interpolate within the square rather than reading the upper-right grid line. Accuracy depends on grid scale and symbol position. Preserve leading zeroes when present.

questions.prompt: Eastings, northings and grid references — A point is 0.6 across from easting 24 toward 25 and 0.2 up from northing 60 toward 61. Write its four-figure and six-figure references.
options: Use the map length directly as kilometres; omit unit conversion.
Reverse the numerator and denominator and omit the stated map scale.
Read eastings first: 24, with sixth-tenth interpolation giving 246. · Read northings: 60, with second-tenth interpolation giving 602. · Area reference 2460; six-figure reference 246602.
questions.explanation: Read eastings first: 24, with sixth-tenth interpolation giving 246. · Read northings: 60, with second-tenth interpolation giving 602. · Area reference 2460; six-figure reference 246602.

questions.prompt: Yasi: physical processes and compound impacts — Which statement accurately explains yasi: physical processes and compound impacts?
options: A cyclone’s pressure and winds can raise coastal water levels; waves add energy at the shoreline. Heavy rain can flood rivers and slopes independently of the wind maximum.
Storm surge is simply another name for heavy rainfall.
A place’s name alone establishes its processes and outcomes.
questions.explanation: Low coastal elevation, coastal shape and tide timing influence inundation. A hillside or river catchment can experience impacts away from landfall. Attribute each consequence to its physical pathway.

questions.prompt: Area from maps and unit conversion — Which statement accurately explains area from maps and unit conversion?
options: A place’s name alone establishes its processes and outcomes.
Area depends on the square of a length scale. One square kilometre is 1,000,000 m² or 100 hectares; one hectare is 10,000 m². Counting grid cells gives an estimate for irregular shapes.
An area scale is identical to the length scale.
questions.explanation: At 1:50,000, 1 cm is 0.5 km, so 1 cm² represents 0.25 km². Edge cells can be estimated by halves; state uncertainty rather than implying perfect precision.

questions.prompt: Human decisions and unequal cyclone vulnerability — Which statement accurately explains human decisions and unequal cyclone vulnerability?
options: Wealth alone removes cyclone vulnerability.
A place’s name alone establishes its processes and outcomes.

Settlement location, construction, income, insurance, communication and transport can intensify or reduce cyclone impacts. Development level is a broad context, not a reliable prediction for every household.
questions.explanation: More resources may improve forecasting, shelters and building enforcement, but inequalities remain within wealthy places. In lower-income places, strong community networks can provide capacity despite limited infrastructure.

questions.prompt: Map conventions, atlas choices and sketch maps — Which statement accurately explains map conventions, atlas choices and sketch maps?
options: A usable map states title, orientation, legend, scale and source, usually within a border. An atlas can supply location and thematic context, but its scale and date determine usefulness.
Every image that looks like a map can be used for accurate measurement.
A place’s name alone establishes its processes and outcomes.
questions.explanation: A sketch map simplifies features to support an argument; symbols and annotations should explain relationships rather than reproduce decoration. A schematic is not suitable for precise distance calculations unless a scale is supplied.

questions.prompt: Mitigation and preparedness — Which statement accurately explains mitigation and preparedness?
options: A place’s name alone establishes its processes and outcomes.
Mitigation reduces potential impacts; preparedness builds the ability to respond and recover before an event. Some actions contribute to both, so explain the mechanism rather than relying on a label.
Issuing a warning guarantees every resident can evacuate.
questions.explanation: Stronger roof connections reduce structural damage; evacuation drills, supplies and communication plans improve readiness. A warning only helps when people receive, understand and can act on it.

questions.prompt: Compass directions and bearings — Which statement accurately explains compass directions and bearings?
options: Bearings are measured anticlockwise from east.
A place’s name alone establishes its processes and outcomes.
Compass direction expresses orientation; a bearing is an angle measured clockwise from north, normally written with three digits. Sixteen-point directions divide the compass into 22.5° sectors.
questions.explanation: East is 090°, south 180° and west 270°. A reverse bearing differs by 180° with adjustment to the 000–359° range. Distinguish grid, true and magnetic north when a map supplies them.

questions.prompt: Recurrence intervals and probability — Which statement accurately explains recurrence intervals and probability?
options: A recurrence interval is a long-run average interval between events at or above a specified magnitude; it is not a timetable. A 1-in-100-year event has a 1% annual exceedance probability under the assumed stationary model.
A 50-year flood cannot happen again until 50 years have passed.
A place’s name alone establishes its processes and outcomes.
questions.explanation: For independent years with constant annual probability p, the chance of at least one event in n years is 1 − (1 − p)^n. Climate or land-use changes can invalidate a stationary estimate.

questions.prompt: Contours, landforms and slope shape — Which statement accurately explains contours, landforms and slope shape?
options: A place’s name alone establishes its processes and outcomes.

Mitigation reduces potential impacts; preparedness builds the ability to respond and recover before an event. Some actions contribute to both, so explain the mechanism rather than relying on a label.
questions.explanation: Stronger roof connections reduce structural damage; evacuation drills, supplies and communication plans improve readiness. A warning only helps when people receive, understand and can act on it.

questions.prompt: Compass directions and bearings — Which statement accurately explains compass directions and bearings?
options: Compass direction expresses orientation; a bearing is an angle measured clockwise from north, normally written with three digits. Sixteen-point directions divide the compass into 22.5° sectors.
Bearings are measured anticlockwise from east.
A place’s name alone establishes its processes and outcomes.
questions.explanation: East is 090°, south 180° and west 270°. A reverse bearing differs by 180° with adjustment to the 000–359° range. Distinguish grid, true and magnetic north when a map supplies them.

questions.prompt: Recurrence intervals and probability — Which statement accurately explains recurrence intervals and probability?
options: A place’s name alone establishes its processes and outcomes.

A recurrence interval is a long-run average interval between events at or above a specified magnitude; it is not a timetable. A 1-in-100-year event has a 1% annual exceedance probability under the assumed stationary model.
A 50-year flood cannot happen again until 50 years have passed.
questions.explanation: For independent years with constant annual probability p, the chance of at least one event in n years is 1 − (1 − p)^n. Climate or land-use changes can invalidate a stationary estimate.

questions.prompt: Eastings, northings and grid references — Which statement accurately explains eastings, northings and grid references?
options: Northings are read before eastings.
A place’s name alone establishes its processes and outcomes.

Grid references identify positions on a mapped grid. Read eastings first, then northings. A four-figure area reference identifies a square; a six-figure reference estimates a point to tenths within it.
questions.explanation: For a six-figure reference, interpolate within the square rather than reading the upper-right grid line. Accuracy depends on grid scale and symbol position. Preserve leading zeroes when present.

questions.prompt: Latitude, longitude and degrees–minutes — Which statement accurately explains latitude, longitude and degrees–minutes?
options: Latitude measures angular distance north or south of the equator; longitude measures angular distance east or west of the prime meridian. One degree contains 60 minutes, not 100.
Minutes can be converted by dividing by 100.
A place’s name alone establishes its processes and outcomes.
questions.explanation: A coordinate needs hemisphere or signed convention. Angular differences are not automatically equal ground distances: longitude distance changes with latitude. Latitude-longitude is different from a local grid reference.

questions.prompt: Hazards, risk and disasters — Which statement accurately explains hazards, risk and disasters?
options: A place’s name alone establishes its processes and outcomes.

A hazard is a potentially damaging process; risk depends on the chance of an event and its consequences for exposed people and assets. A disaster is a severe disruption when impacts exceed a community’s capacity to cope.
A severe hazard always creates the same disaster everywhere.
questions.explanation: Exposure locates people or assets in harm’s way; vulnerability describes susceptibility; capacity includes resources to prepare and recover. The same physical event can produce different losses in two places.

questions.prompt: Yasi: environmental, economic and social impacts — Which statement accurately explains yasi: environmental, economic and social impacts?
options: An impact can belong to only one category.
A place’s name alone establishes its processes and outcomes.

Environmental impacts affect ecosystems; economic impacts affect production, assets and incomes; social impacts affect health, housing, access and wellbeing. One loss can have consequences across categories.
questions.explanation: Damage to vegetation may reduce habitat, interrupt farming and affect household employment. Distinguish direct immediate damage from indirect consequences such as supply-chain disruption and stress.

questions.prompt: Dengue vulnerability and human amplification — Which statement accurately explains dengue vulnerability and human amplification?
options: Water storage, waste, drainage, housing and access to health services can alter dengue exposure and outcomes. These interact with seasonal conditions and mosquito ecology.
People in a poorer place are all equally vulnerable.
A place’s name alone establishes its processes and outcomes.
questions.explanation: Uncovered containers can create breeding sites; delayed diagnosis can increase the risk of severe outcomes. Distinguish a mechanism supported by evidence from blaming residents for infrastructure constraints.

questions.prompt: Yasi-context strategy evaluation: stronger buildings — Which statement accurately explains yasi-context strategy evaluation: stronger buildings?
options: A place’s name alone establishes its processes and outcomes.
Structural mitigation aims to reduce damage from a specified hazard pathway. Evaluate its effectiveness, affordability, equity and environmental consequences rather than listing features.
Wind-resistant construction also guarantees protection from every flood.
questions.explanation: Roof-to-wall connections and maintained building envelopes can reduce wind damage. A wind-resistant building may still be vulnerable to surge or river flooding, so site planning matters.

questions.prompt: Comparing natural and ecological risk management — Which statement accurately explains comparing natural and ecological risk management?
options: The same mitigation measure will work for every hazard.
A place’s name alone establishes its processes and outcomes.
Natural and ecological hazards can share exposure and inequality patterns but have different agents, timelines and controls. Compare mechanisms rather than applying one solution to all hazards.
questions.explanation: Cyclone shelter planning manages acute physical danger; dengue source reduction manages breeding and transmission over repeated cycles. Both need inclusive communication, reliable services and evaluation.

questions.prompt: Atmospheric, hydrological and geomorphic hazards — Which statement accurately explains atmospheric, hydrological and geomorphic hazards?
options: Atmospheric hazards arise from weather processes; hydrological hazards involve water movement or availability; geomorphic hazards involve Earth materials and landforms. Boundaries can overlap in a compound event.
Each event belongs to one isolated category with no linked hazards.
A place’s name alone establishes its processes and outcomes.
questions.explanation: A tropical cyclone is atmospheric, river flooding is hydrological and a landslide is geomorphic. Drought develops through prolonged water shortage; bushfire involves fuel, weather and ignition rather than a single category alone.

questions.prompt: Contours, landforms and slope shape — Which statement is a misconception to correct?
options: Methods should be appropriate to the question and data.
Every closed contour must be a hill, regardless of map symbols.
A supported conclusion should identify its evidence and scope.
questions.explanation: Contours join points of equal elevation. Close spacing indicates a steeper slope for the same contour interval; valleys and spurs have different contour shapes. Spot heights give point elevations. A valley’s contour V usually points uphill; a spur’s projection points downhill. Concave slopes steepen uphill and flatten toward the foot; convex slopes are gentler near the top and steeper lower down.

questions.prompt: Coffee supply chains and value capture — Which statement accurately explains coffee supply chains and value capture?
options: A supply chain links growing, processing, exporting, shipping, roasting and retailing. Value capture describes which actors retain revenue after their costs, not simply the final sale price.
The retailer earns a $24 profit whenever the farmer receives $4.
A place’s name alone establishes its processes and outcomes.
questions.explanation: Transformation, branding, distribution and market access can concentrate earnings downstream. Farmers’ income also depends on yield, quality, labour costs and bargaining arrangements.

questions.prompt: World cities as command and cultural nodes — Which statement accurately explains world cities as command and cultural nodes?

World cities are important nodes in international networks of finance, corporate services, transport, communication and culture. Their influence is not determined solely by population size.
Every megacity is automatically a leading world city.
questions.explanation: Corporate headquarters coordinate investment; specialised services support global business; media and institutions distribute ideas. Smaller influential cities can have stronger global functions than larger cities.

questions.prompt: Graphs, correlation and causal claims — Which statement accurately explains graphs, correlation and causal claims?
options: A strong correlation establishes a causal mechanism without other evidence.
A place’s name alone establishes its processes and outcomes.
Graph choice depends on data: lines for ordered time, bars for categories, histograms for grouped continuous values, scatterplots for association, and population pyramids for age-sex structure.

questions.prompt: Institutions, corporations and football networks — Which statement accurately explains institutions, corporations and football networks?
options: Transnational sporting institutions coordinate rules, tournaments and development; corporations sponsor, broadcast and market events. Their roles influence cultural spread and who receives resources.
An institution’s promotional claim is sufficient evidence of programme success.
A place’s name alone establishes its processes and outcomes.
questions.explanation: Development programmes can improve coaching and club organisation; sponsors may prioritise large markets. FIFA’s material can document stated programmes but cannot alone prove their local effects.

questions.prompt: Transport and time–space compression — Which statement accurately explains transport and time–space compression?

Time–space compression describes reductions in the time or cost of connecting places. It changes functional distance without changing their actual kilometres apart.
Faster transport is always the most sustainable choice.
questions.explanation: Containerisation standardises cargo handling; refrigeration preserves perishable goods; air transport speeds selected flows. Ports and logistics hubs concentrate movement and can create bottlenecks.

questions.prompt: Telecommunications and digital inequalities — Which statement accurately explains telecommunications and digital inequalities?

A place’s name alone establishes its processes and outcomes.

questions.explanation: Digital platforms can connect small enterprises to consumers and international organisations. Algorithms and platform ownership influence visibility, while unequal broadband access can limit participation.

questions.prompt: Diffusion, adoption and adaptation — Which statement accurately explains diffusion, adoption and adaptation?
options: Diffusion is the spread of an idea or practice between places. Adoption accepts it; adaptation changes it to fit local needs. Expansion diffusion spreads outward while relocation diffusion moves with people.
Cultural diffusion only produces identical practices everywhere.
A place’s name alone establishes its processes and outcomes.
questions.explanation: Contagious diffusion spreads through contact; hierarchical diffusion can move through influential centres; migration carries practices to new destinations. Multiple processes can operate together.

questions.prompt: Governments and enterprises in coffee distribution — Which statement accurately explains governments and enterprises in coffee distribution?

Only consumers influence where a commodity is produced.
questions.explanation: A processing investment can create local jobs and retain more value, but needs skills, energy and buyers. Certification can change practices while imposing costs that some growers cannot afford.

questions.prompt: Football as an element of culture — Which statement accurately explains football as an element of culture?

questions.prompt: Change statistics, descriptive statistics and frequency — Which statement accurately explains change statistics, descriptive statistics and frequency?

A rise from 40% to 60% is always described accurately as a 20% increase.
A place’s name alone establishes its processes and outcomes.

questions.explanation: Tracking can connect batch quality and origin records to buyers; shipping reliability affects delivery and inventory. Poor last-mile roads can remain a barrier even when global ships are efficient.

questions.prompt: Global networks inquiry and evidence-based writing — Which statement accurately explains global networks inquiry and evidence-based writing?

A place’s name alone establishes its processes and outcomes.

questions.prompt: Coffee as a global commodity — Which statement accurately explains coffee as a global commodity?

questions.prompt: Population pyramids, climate graphs and synoptic charts — Which statement accurately explains population pyramids, climate graphs and synoptic charts?

A place’s name alone establishes its processes and outcomes.

A population pyramid shows age structure split by sex or gender categories defined by its source; a climate graph shows monthly temperature and rainfall; a synoptic chart shows pressure and weather systems at a time.
questions.explanation: Compare units and denominators in pyramids; annual rainfall is the sum of monthly rainfall and temperature range is maximum minus minimum monthly mean. Close isobars suggest a stronger pressure gradient, not an exact wind speed.

questions.prompt: Social, economic and environmental globalisation impacts — Which statement accurately explains social, economic and environmental globalisation impacts?

A place’s name alone establishes its processes and outcomes.
questions.explanation: An export boom may raise revenue yet concentrate profits among processors. Transport creates emissions; specialised production can pressure land or water. Cultural exchange can support creativity and threaten some local practices.

questions.prompt: Media, technology and football’s cultural reach — Which statement accurately explains media, technology and football’s cultural reach?

Broadcasting, streaming and social platforms can increase visibility, connect supporters and circulate symbols. Media influence includes whose competitions are shown and who can afford access.
More video views prove the same percentage increase in players.
questions.explanation: Algorithms, rights agreements and language affect audience reach. Mobile highlights can connect supporters quickly, yet participation still requires facilities, time and safe access.

questions.prompt: Global networks inquiry and evidence-based writing — Which statement accurately explains global networks inquiry and evidence-based writing?
options: One chart can fully prove all consequences of globalisation.
A place’s name alone establishes its processes and outcomes.
An inquiry into globalisation needs a defined flow, places, period and measure. Combine quantitative patterns with stakeholder evidence and explain limitations.
questions.explanation: Trade data, maps, interviews and media accounts answer different questions. A flow map can show connections but not necessarily profit, fairness or cultural meaning.

questions.prompt: Coffee as a global commodity — Which statement accurately explains coffee as a global commodity?
options: Coffee links tropical growing areas, traders, roasters, retailers and consumers. Production suitability and consumption demand create a geography of interdependence rather than a single local market.
A country exporting processed coffee must grow all of those beans.
A place’s name alone establishes its processes and outcomes.
questions.explanation: Physical conditions shape cultivation; infrastructure, skills and markets shape processing and trade. FAO identifies climate change and the economic sustainability of production as important industry uncertainties.

questions.prompt: Population pyramids, climate graphs and synoptic charts — Which statement accurately explains population pyramids, climate graphs and synoptic charts?
options: A place’s name alone establishes its processes and outcomes.

A population pyramid shows age structure split by sex or gender categories defined by its source; a climate graph shows monthly temperature and rainfall; a synoptic chart shows pressure and weather systems at a time.
A single synoptic chart represents the long-term climate.
questions.explanation: Compare units and denominators in pyramids; annual rainfall is the sum of monthly rainfall and temperature range is maximum minus minimum monthly mean. Close isobars suggest a stronger pressure gradient, not an exact wind speed.

questions.prompt: Graphs, correlation and causal claims — Which statement accurately explains graphs, correlation and causal claims?

A strong correlation establishes a causal mechanism without other evidence.
A place’s name alone establishes its processes and outcomes.
questions.explanation: Correlation describes co-variation, not proof of cause. Shared drivers, reverse causation and sampling can produce associations. Climate graphs combine rainfall columns and temperature lines with separate axes.
